messages:
jordan: FYI — ACME in prod just raised an escalation. After today's 06:00 UTC rollout their templated classification output regressed. A tiny change (adding a trailing period) causes a completely different class. They say failure rate jumped from ~0.5% to ~30% across three templates. Pasting their minimal repro below and asking for triage.

acme_support: Confirmed. Minimal test cases attached by customer: changing 'Please approve request' -> 'Please approve request.' flips from APPROVE -> REJECT. Happens for multiple user templates, across regions. No other obvious input changes.

jordan: @ashok can you check canary history + whether any tokenizer/normalization changes shipped in the rollout? We rolled model variant redwood/gpt-opt-3.2-q4 at 06:00.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout complete for model: redwood/gpt-opt-3.2-q4 at 2026-03-10T06:00:12Z canary=10% -> 100%

ashok: On it. Can you paste the exact API call + prompt variations? Need the exact bytes so I can reproduce tokenization locally.

acme_support: Here's their curl repro (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" 
 -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-opt-3.2-q4","prompt":"Please approve request","max_tokens":32}'
```
and
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" 
 -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-opt-3.2-q4","prompt":"Please approve request.","max_tokens":32}'
```
They also said replacing the trailing period with a space or newline sometimes changes the result.

kelly: This smells like tokenization / token-boundary sensitivity. Trailing punctuation can change tokenization (different token ids, different alignment with learned position embeddings / soft prompts). But a 30% jump suggests something else (kernel change, quantization, or template normalization). Any changes to the prompt templating or tokenizer in this rollout?

ashok: No explicit tokenizer model change in the repo. BUT we did flip to a newer quantized kernel variant to speed up decoding (PR #1289) and a minor trimming change in the templating pipeline was merged earlier this week (PR #1472). I'm running a local repro against the same binary to compare token ids and outputs.

jordan: Customer also reported latency increased ~1.5x post-rollout for these requests. Could be batching or kernel perf regressions as well.

ashok: Quick trace log from a failing request (sanitized):
`tokenized_prompt_without_period: [154, 78, 909, 2]`
`tokenized_prompt_with_period:    [154, 78, 909, 43]`
Response (without period): APPROVE
Response (with period):    REJECT
Notice the last token id changes 2 -> 43. I'm digging into the kernel step where we compute attention masks + kv cache offsets; small token offset could change cached key alignment if there's an off-by-one in the new kernel's cache handling.

kelly: If the new kernel has a different expectation for EOS/padding handling that could easily flip logits for boundary tokens. Also check whether we inadvertently changed tokenizer.normalizer or unicode normalization in the template pipeline (that PR you mentioned, @ashok).

jordan: The templating PR trimmed trailing whitespace by default. Could remove an invisible char in customer's templates. @ashok can you grep for 'normalize' or 'trim' usage in the service binary?

ashok: Grep shows: `if (allow_trim) normalize_unicode(prompt);` — the conditional was set true in the canary config. I'm reverting canary to 10% and will roll back the kernel change to isolate. Pushing change now.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated for model redwood/gpt-opt-3.2-q4 -> redwood/gpt-opt-3.1 at 2026-03-10T06:26:17Z (canary 10%)

acme_support: Quick update from ACME after we flipped them to the previous variant: they re-ran the same tests and report behavior returned to baseline (failure ~1%). They also noted the latency returned to previous levels.

jordan: Good. Action items: 1) Run A/B test focused on tokenization edge-cases across templating changes (assign @kelly). 2) Add a token-level debug flag in SDK/console to show tokenization diff for customers (assign @ashok). 3) Add explicit unit tests covering trailing punctuation/newline/space variants in templating engine. 4) Draft incident update for the customer and internal postmortem.

kelly: I'll add unit tests + a small opt-out flag for the new kernel until we have kernel verified across token-boundary cases. I'll also add test vectors from ACME into our eval suite.

jordan: Thanks everyone. I'll keep CS and the customer updated. We'll post a follow-up in #incidents once we have RCA. :white_check_mark:
